articles.title: China's Xi arrives in Washington, kicking off his state visit with rare planeside welcome from Trump
articles.summary:
STORY: EDITORS NOTE: THIS HAS BEEN REFILED TO AMEND THE VIDEO'S DIGITAL RESTRICTIONS TO 'NO EDITS PERMITTED' FROM 'NO USE USA.' NO CHANGES TO VIDEO.

:: Washington, D.C.

:: Trevor Hunnicutt, White House Correspondent

"So it's the four Ts: trade, technology, Tehran, and Taiwan. Those are going to be the big important topics that come out of this meeting. Whether or not these two leaders can actually agree on these topics and make progress towards having the two most powerful countries in the world on the same page."

"The U.S. has a legal responsibility to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself, and that includes providing arms sales to Taiwan."

:: That's what Xi Jinping wants to stop

"That's what Xi Jinping wants to stop, and he made a very clear point of this in May, the last time he met Donald Trump in Beijing. He said, 'This needs to stop. Taiwan is an aggressor. They are a threat to peace.'"

"So China has been having for years an economic problem, right? They’ve had this kind of long-term property collapse. They’ve had very weak domestic demand where people there just aren’t buying the things that they’re making."

"Even though those problems still exist, China's been able to turbocharge its exports, its manufacturing. It's selling to the whole world, to Latin America, to Asia, to Europe, and yes, to the United States, even though Trump has put these tariffs on Chinese imports. And so that's really allowed Xi to kind of come into this meeting with a very strong hand."

"Both sides have signaled very low expectations. Don't expect a grand reset or a grand bargain or some kind of major shift in policy on either side. But you could have deals around the edges. You could have agreements for the U.S. and China to start talking about things like AI that they haven't really been substantively talking about before."

"One thing we'll be watching for is just what the tone is like from these leaders. President Trump has primarily been very positive, talking about how he has a great relationship with Xi. But then he also gave a primetime address a couple of months ago where he accused China of meddling in U.S. elections."

:: July 16, 2026

"The People's Republic of China carried out what is believed to be the largest compromise of election data in history."

"So what's the tone like? Which Trump do we get for this meeting?"
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington on Wednesday, where he was met with a rare planeside greeting from President Donald Trump , who was there to welcome his counterpart instead of waiting for him to drive up to the White House.

Trump's decision to greet Xi at Joint Base Andrews just outside Washington rather than receiving him at the executive residence shows how far the U.S. president is going to honor China's leader as he made his first state visit to the U.S. capital in more than a decade.

A 100-foot (30 meter) long red carpet was unfurled at the bottom of the staircase placed at the door of Xi's plane. A 21-person honor guard was arrayed on the sides of the carpet and Trump and first lady Melania Trump stood near a staircase on the side of the plane, where they greeted Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, with handshakes.

Two American children presented bouquets of yellow-colored flowers to Xi and his wife. The welcome ceremony also included a flyover by two B-1 bombers, platoons from each military service, and a presentation of the flags and anthems of both countries. Trump and his wife spoke to their counterparts, but their words could not be heard. Trump, who wore gloves and an overcoat though it was a relatively warm 63 degrees Fahrenheit (17 degrees Celsius) outside, removed one of his gloves to shake hands with Xi. At one point, he slapped Xi on the back and said something to him that was inaudible.

The salutation kicks off a three-day visit that's expected to be saturated with pomp, even by White House standards. The state visit, complete with a formal state dinner at the White House on Thursday, is supposed to reciprocate the ceremonial grandeur that marked Trump's May visit to China.

But it also is a showy patina at a time when tensions between the two geopolitical rivals are high over trade, artificial intelligence, Trump's war with Iran and China's designs on Taiwan .

The visit comes after Trump's trip to China in May

Beyond using the visit to try to keep "strategic stability" between the two countries, Trump seems to be pulling out all the diplomatic stops to show off for Xi. Trump has lavished praise on Xi as a "great leader" and described a warm relationship with the man he has called a friend. That is all while he has given Xi a pass on many issues .

Sen. Roger Wicker, chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, criticized the "lavish welcome." Wicker, R-Miss., said during a speech Tuesday in the Senate that Trump should not have invited the Chinese leader "based on all of the troubling issues we have with President Xi and the Chinese Communist Party."

Wicker archly suggested a list of topics that Trump could discuss with Xi at the state dinner, such as "the purposes of China's massive military buildup, or about China's clear support for Iran," saying that "during every minute of dialogue" Trump should keep in mind that "his guest is a brutal, unelected and oppressive dictator who seeks to dominate his neighbors and whose massive military arsenal is aimed directly at the United States of America."

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the U.S. and China must interact at the highest levels because the countries are "the two largest economies in the world" and "probably the two most powerful militaries in the world."

"The idea that we would not interact with them at the highest levels is irresponsible. It's outrageous. We have to," Rubio told reporters Wednesday while he was in New York.

Trump to welcome Xi with 'the most respect'

Trump has made it clear he wants to wow Xi , telling reporters in recent weeks that he was delighted his new "work of art" helicopter landing pad would be ready for the visit while bemoaning that his massive White House ballroom would not.

Trump on Wednesday was looking to match the pageantry he was met with in China earlier this year. Xi was not at the airport to meet Trump — Chinese Vice President Han Zheng was there instead. But a red carpet was rolled out to meet Air Force One in Beijing. A military honor guard, a military band and about 300 Chinese youths waving Chinese and American flags and chanting, "Welcome, welcome! Warm welcome!" also were present. The children wore white and light blue uniforms that mirrored the traditional paint colors of the presidential plane.

The first lady said earlier Wednesday that her husband decided to personally greet Xi when he arrived in the Washington region because "they have a great relationship."

"He's coming on our soil, and we need to welcome them with the most respect," she said of Xi and his wife during an interview on Fox News Channel's "Fox & Friends."

The long red carpet recalled a similar extra-long one the U.S. laid out for Russian President Vladimir Putin when he touched down at a U.S. Air Force base in Alaska last summer for a summit aimed at trying to find an end to Russia's war in Ukraine.

When Putin arrived in August 2025, he shook hands with Trump while both grinned. They then took the unusual step of climbing into Trump's limo to share a ride to the building where they were holding talks.

On Wednesday at the end of the arrival ceremony, Xi and his wife climbed into their own car, and the Trumps retreated to theirs.

A black-tie dinner and visit to the archives will follow

Trump's airport ceremony for Xi will be followed on Thursday by more formalities, including an arrival ceremony at the White House and a review of troops. Before the black-tie dinner, which will feature tech industry leaders like Nvidia's Jensen Huang and SpaceX's Elon Musk , the two leaders are expected to dive into the weighty issues behind closed doors, even as expectations are low that the trip will produce any major breakthroughs in the relationship.

On Friday, Xi and Peng will be back at the White House for a private tea with the Trumps before joining them on a tour of the National Archives in Washington. The White House has said they will view historic documents underscoring the relationship between the two countries.

Associated Press writers Mary Clare Jalonick, Will Weissert and Didi Tang contributed to this report.

articles.title: Family tied to suspected Chinese spy gave $4.4M to Newsom, Calif. politicians
articles.summary: C.C. Yin's family has donated nearly $3 million to state-level California political causes and an additional $1,455,027 to federal campaigns.
articles.body:
A California family gave over $4.4 million in political donations to Governor Gavin Newsom, Kamala Harris and other leading California politicians. And now, that family's alleged past links to infamous suspected honeypot spy Fang Fang, also known as Christine Fang, and other Chinese government officials have thrust them into an ongoing debate over foreign influence in American politics.

The Yin family made millions running McDonald's franchises in the Golden State — and became prolific donors to politicians, according to state and federal campaign records. Newly released FBI files about Fang describe the family patriarch Chei Chen Yin, commonly known by his initials "C.C.", as a one-time professional associate of Fang through an organization he founded.

And national security experts tasked with protecting U.S. institutions from infiltration by the Chinese government say they have documented alleged interactions between C.C. Yin's brother, Henry Yin, and the foreign influence wing of the Chinese government, the United Front.

Interactions between wealthy business leaders with direct ties to China have come under heavier scrutiny in recent years, as a series of scandals have erupted over alleged Chinese influence agents gaining access to elected officials from small town mayors to members of Congress and the governor of New York . Those relationships have often been facilitated with political donations.

Jacqueline Deal, a board member of State Armor, a company that helps lawmakers detect foreign influence operations, told CBS News that the Chinese government has a "broad-reaching, coordinated strategy for dominance that relies on shaping U.S. policy so that over time we get weaker and [China] gets stronger."

She said she suspects political donations are being used to help "disincentivize these leaders from noticing Chinese Communist Party political interference." There is no evidence the Yins have been co-opted in this way.

C.C. Yin told CBS News: "I love America, and I strongly condemn any effort by any foreign government to interfere in American politics or undermine our democracy." Henry Yin did not respond to requests for comment.

Yin family donated millions to political causes

C.C. Yin, 89, is known in Northern California for his philanthropy and rags-to-riches story of a Chinese immigrant arriving to the U.S. in the 1960s with just $100 and building a successful franchise business.

He and his brother Henry Yin founded and ran an organization called Asian Pacific American Public Affairs, or APAPA, organizing support for favored political candidates and helping place interns and advisers in the offices of local, state and federal officials, according to APAPA's website.

C.C. Yin told CBS News he started APAPA to help "young people and community members develop leadership skills, understand how government works, vote, serve their communities, and participate in our democracy."

"When this country gives us opportunity, we have a responsibility to give back," he said.

Some of the Yins' giving has come in the form of large political donations.

The family has donated nearly $3 million to state-level California political causes and an additional $1,455,027 to federal campaigns, directly and through C.C. Yin's McDonald's franchise business, according to state and Federal Election Commission records.

This includes $364,817 in donations to past campaigns supporting Gavin Newsom, $80,000 to his 2019 inauguration committee and $50,000 to a nonprofit at Newsom's direction.

The Yins as individuals and C.C. Yin's McDonald's franchise also gave California Lt. Gov. Eleni Kounalakis' campaigns $221,700 between 2018 and 2025, state records show. Former Vice President Kamala Harris' campaigns received $214,300 between 2019 and 2024, and former state Treasurer John Chiang's campaigns received $115,680.

FBI files declassified by the White House in August point to a previous close working relationship between C.C. Yin and suspected Chinese spy Fang "Christine" Fang, who had a sexual relationship with disgraced former California congressman Eric Swalwell before fleeing to China in 2015.

The files include Swalwell's interviews with the FBI in 2015 and 2016, in which he identified Fang as his "point of contact" for APAPA. In one interview Swalwell said a top APAPA official directed him to Fang, according to the files. That official's name is redacted in the report, but two sources familiar with its content told CBS News it is C.C. Yin.

Fang appeared alongside C.C. Yin and Henry Yin at a 15-person APAPA event, in a photo posted on Facebook in 2013 by a City of Cupertino official.

APAPA president Kris Concepcion told CBS News that "current leadership is not aware of Fang Fang ever holding an official role with the national organization."

"Our understanding is that she was associated with a local chapter that is no longer operational," he said. "Like hundreds, or even thousands, of other community members who attend public events, being photographed with APAPA members does not mean she was an officer, board member, employee or representative of APAPA."

No evidence has emerged that Henry Yin or C.C. Yin knew about Fang's alleged espionage during her involvement in APAPA.

After noticing APAPA's connection with Fang Fang, Deal dug into the background of Henry Yin, who previously served as national board chair of APAPA and is currently a board member.

She found a string of Chinese media reports of his attendance at 10 events in China hosted by officials from the Chinese government and its foreign influence wing, the United Front, since 2013. The United Front published Chinese-language write-ups of Henry Yin's reported meetings in 2015 and 2023.

Henry Yin has described his efforts as "networking." Deal said his relationship with China "seems to be one of open cooperation."

One article said Yin traveled to Baoshan in Yunnan province in June 2015 and held talks with the Municipal Party Committee United Front Work Department, reaching "a consensus on further strengthening contacts." It described Yin as their "designated contact person for California–China economic, trade, scientific and technological interaction".

Another 2013 article by a Chinese government office described a meeting between Yin and a Chinese government official in Chengdu, capital of Sichuan province, saying that he had been offered a position there with the title "Overseas Talent Recruitment Adviser for Sichuan Province." There is no evidence Yin accepted that offer, which was made during a friendlier time in U.S.-China relations.

A United Front statement from 2023 said a delegation of "Chinese Entrepreneurs from Silicon Valley" including Henry Yin, visited his hometown of Chengdu and "built a new bridge for investment cooperation between Chengdu and Silicon Valley."

Henry Yin told the East Bay Times in 2016, while he was serving on the California Commission for Economic Development, that his goal was to further business relations between China and the U.S., as part of his decades as a trans-national entrepreneur.

"I've done a lot of networking, and these days I'm glad to see these networks deliver results," he told the newspaper.

Neither Henry Yin nor his brother have been accused by U.S. law enforcement of working as a foreign agent or acting against American interests.

Foreign Policy Research Institute fellow and University of Miami professor June Teufel Dreyer told CBS News that, although political donations and advisory roles are patterns of influence used by the United Front, those actions and traveling to China for diplomacy and business trips could be entirely innocent.

"There's really nothing wrong with successful Chinese entrepreneurs wanting to help out the economies of the country they originally came from," Dreyer said, but added: "We should get rid of the idea that there's such a thing as a truly private business in China. They are all controlled at some level by the government."

Cheryl Yu, a fellow at foreign affairs think tank The Jamestown Foundation, told CBS News that the Chinese government attempts to exert influence on well-connected Americans, regardless of those individuals' intentions.

"This is how the United Front works. They build these friendly, long-term relationships, then at some point they make requests," she said.

The U.S. government has allegedly engaged in its own influence attempts against China, including a clandestine social media campaign to turn public opinion in China against President Xi Jinping's government, a 2024 Reuters report claimed .

Concepcion said his organization has "no relationship with the People's Republic of China, the Chinese Communist Party, or the United Front," and that "personal travel, relationships, employment histories, and views" of members "should not be attributed to APAPA."

The Yins' foreign and domestic connections have at times placed them at the nexus of Chinese diplomacy and American politics.

C.C. Yin was credited with helping arrange Newsom's 2023 trip to China according to a story co-authored by his organization in New York-based Taiwanese newspaper the World Journal.

The newspaper article said that C.C. Yin began negotiating the visit "after being entrusted by the governor's office" to "formally [convey] Governor Newsom's desire to visit China to Consul General Zhang Jianmin."

His brother Henry Yin accompanied the governor as an adviser on the October 2023 visit, where Newsom met Chinese President Xi Jinping, the Journal reported.

Henry Yin has also been photographed with Newsom at APAPA events, which he shared on Facebook.

Newsom's spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment. The governor is among those expected to seek the 2028 Democratic nomination for president.

Henry Yin also acted as an adviser to California congressman Ro Khanna, who is similarly talked about as a potential Democratic 2028 presidential candidate and is currently the ranking member of the House Select Committee on the CCP, established with the purpose of monitoring Chinese government influence in U.S. politics. Henry Yin and C.C. Yin have personally donated $15,800 to Khanna's congressional campaigns since 2017.

Khanna's spokesperson has since given statements about Henry Yin's relationship with the influential lawmaker that conflict with Khanna's own social media posts.

A 2019 Facebook post by Khanna included a photo of Henry Yin presenting the congressman with a birthday cake, with the caption announcing that "Henry will serve as my Senior Advisor on Foreign Trade and Economic Development." In a 2020 post he referred to Henry Yin as a "good friend."

Until this month, Yin listed on his LinkedIn page a current role as "Sr. Advisor to US House of Rep [Ro] Khanna," beginning in 2019. The page has since been deleted.

Khanna appeared alongside Henry in February this year at a Sunnyvale, California event run by APAPA-affiliated PAC, Asian Americans for Good Government. Both Henry Yin and C.C. Yin have been listed as board members of the PAC, according to archives of its website .

Earlier this month, his spokesperson told the New York Post that Henry Yin "has never held a formal role with the Congressman." In a subsequent statement to CBS News, Khanna's communications director Sarah Drory said that Henry Yin "served for a year as one of dozens of volunteer leaders."

Drory added in the statement that "APAPA has been a decades-long organization to empower Asian Americans and it's an ugly anti-Asian smear to suggest ties" to the Chinese government.

articles.title: Father of 9/11 hero Todd Beamer appears in Michigan Senate race ad to condemn Hasan Piker rhetoric
articles.summary: David Beamer, father of Flight 93 hero Todd Beamer, appeared in a campaign ad for Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers condemning Hasan Piker and...
articles.body:
David Beamer, father of 9/11 hero Todd Beamer, criticized streamer Hasan Piker and Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed in a campaign video supporting El-Sayed's Republican opponent Mike Rogers.

The video, produced by the Great Lakes Conservative Fund, featured clips of Piker's controversial remarks about 9/11, El-Sayed appearing on Piker's Twitch livestream, and El-Sayed's refusal to disavow Piker.

Former Republican National Committee spokesperson Elizabeth Pipko expressed disappointment that families of 9/11 victims like Todd Beamer's still have to be politically involved to protect their loved ones' legacies.

David Beamer, father of Flight 93 passenger and 9/11 hero Todd Beamer, criticized streamer Hasan Piker and his ties to Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed in a campaign video released Monday for El-Sayed's Republican opponent Mike Rogers.

The video, posted by Great Lakes HQ, was produced by the Great Lakes Conservative Fund, a super PAC supporting Rogers. It began with a 2019 clip of Piker saying that America " deserved 9/11 " followed by clips of El-Sayed appearing on Piker's Twitch livestream and another of El-Sayed refusing to disavow Piker when prompted.

Beamer, who narrates the ad, then introduced his son Todd Beamer, one of the heroes of United Flight 93 who fought back against the terrorists who hijacked the plane in the terror attacks on September 11, 2001.

"Those 43 people on Flight 93 were not victims. They were killed in action. When I hear anyone suggest America 'deserves 9/11' my question is, 'Who would say that?'" Beamer says in the ad.

El-Sayed has repeatedly rejected Piker's 9/11 remark but has resisted calls to completely renounce the streamer, who campaigned with him during the Democratic primary.

Elizabeth Pipko, a former Republican National Committee spokesperson, lamented that families mourning loved ones lost on 9/11 still have to be politically involved to protect their loved ones' legacies.

"How incredibly disappointing that, 25 years after those horrific attacks, Todd Beamer's family is still unable to simply mourn their son and speak about his heroism. Instead, they find themselves having to teach their fellow Americans a lesson they themselves wish they never had to learn," she told Fox News Digital.

"Todd Beamer's family knows better than most the pain that anti-American sentiment and terrorism can inflict on us all. Todd's character, and the American spirit of grit and guts he embodied, is what we should not only remember, but also look for in the leaders we elect to serve our great country," she added further. "In honor of Todd Beamer and all the brave Americans taken from us too soon, we have a job to do — in November and beyond."

Theo Wold, a former assistant attorney general and former White House deputy assistant for domestic policy under Trump, told Fox News Digital that Piker will continue to haunt El-Sayed's campaign as long as the candidate "refuses to denounce" Piker entirely.

"Antifa Democrats and their friends in the media say a lot of dangerous and incendiary things. Hasan Piker, who endorses political violence and has denigrated the Americans killed on September 11th, has repeatedly campaigned alongside his friend El Sayed," Wold said. "El Sayed refuses to denounce Piker not just because they're friends but Leftists like them don't believe there are any boundaries when they are pursuing their ideological goals."

Fox News Digital also reached out to a group representing Gold Star Families, El-Sayed's campaign, and Mike Rogers' campaign but did not immediately receive a response.

articles.title: Hunter Biden responds to GOP senator’s request: ‘I’ll sit next to Don Jr. and testify any time’
articles.summary: Hunter Biden, former President Biden’s son, on Tuesday responded to a request from a GOP senator for both himself and President Trump’s son, Donald Trump Jr....
articles.body:
Hunter Biden, former President Biden's son, on Tuesday responded to a request from a GOP senator for both himself and President Trump's son, Donald Trump Jr. to testify before Congress.

"Sen. Curtis of Utah has suggested that Don Jr. and I should testify before Congress," the younger Biden said in a post on the social platform X Tuesday. "I say bring it on. I've already given more than seven hours of sworn testimony. More than three dozen witnesses testified across two chambers."

"I had no foreign business dealings while my father was president. None. I painted paintings, and I still do," he added. "I'll sit next to Don Jr. and testify any time, any place."

Republican Sen. John Curtis (Utah) sent a letter to Senate Judiciary Committee leaders requesting they investigate President Trump's and former President Biden's business dealings and subpoena their sons to testify in front of Congress.

The Utah senator said that reports on foreign interests using the presidents' sons for accessibility to their fathers "raise legitimate questions about foreign access to members of a sitting president's family and whether such a relationship can create actual or perceived expectations of favorable treatment."

Curtis's push to subpoena Trump Jr. was a political earthquake only a few weeks out from this year's midterm elections. The Utah senator's fellow Republicans in the upper chamber have been wary about entering Trump's crosshairs, especially those running for reelection.

Curtis pointed to Hunter Biden's "substantial business with foreign entities, including interests in China and Ukraine, while his father held or sought public office" and recent ProPublica reporting that Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev shelled out a large portion of the expenses for Trump Jr.'s three-day after-wedding party in the Bahamas.

The Hill has reached out to The Trump Organization for comment.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro apresenta notícia-crime sobre Lula no caso Master | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa do candidato do PL acionou o STF e pediu investigação sobre Lula alegando que mensagens atribuídas a Daniel Vorcaro e advogado indicam articulação do banqueiro com o governo federal.
articles.summary: Defesa do candidato do PL acionou o STF e pediu investigação sobre Lula alegando que mensagens atribuídas a Daniel Vorcaro e advogado indicam articulação do banqueiro com o governo federal.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Lula (PT) durante a propaganda eleitoral na TV nesta terça-feira (15). — Foto: Reprodução

A defesa de Flávio Bolsonaro , candidato do PL à Presidência, apresentou nesta quarta-feira (23) uma notícia-crime contra o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva no caso Master. A petição foi encaminhada ao ministro André Mendonça, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), após a divulgação de mensagens trocadas entre o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro e o advogado Walfrido Warde.

A representação se baseia em diálogos atribuídos a Warde e Vorcaro. Em uma das conversas, obtidas pelo jornal O Globo, o advogado relata ter se encontrado com Lula e afirma que o presidente teria agradecido o envio de uma garrafa de uísque pelo banqueiro.

No documento, a defesa solicita que o caso seja encaminhado à Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) e que seja instaurado um inquérito para apurar condutas que, segundo a peça, podem configurar, em tese, os crimes de corrupção passiva e advocacia administrativa.

“Em razão disso, com base nas mensagens recentemente divulgadas pela mídia, é possível concluir, ao menos em tese, que o Presidente Lula teria utilizado de seu cargo de Presidente da República como forma de atender interesses ilícitos de Daniel Vorcaro junto ao Governo Federal, inclusive mediante o recebimento de vantagem indevida (presentes)”, diz o documento.

Procurada pelo g1 , a defesa do presidente Lula ainda não se pronunciou sobre a notícia-crime apresentada por Flávio Bolsonaro.

Segundo reportagem do jornal O Globo, o advogado Walfrido Warde, que até janeiro deste ano integrava a defesa de Daniel Vorcaro, mencionou, em uma conversa de WhatsApp com o então dono do Banco Master, um suposto uísque dado de presente ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. As mensagens fazem parte do acervo extraído do celular de Vorcaro e foram obtidas pelo jornal.

O diálogo ocorreu 49 dias após a reunião entre Lula e Vorcaro no Palácio do Planalto, em 4 de dezembro de 2024. Segundo a reportagem, Warde afirmou ainda que o presidente “mandou um abraço” para o banqueiro.

O encontro não constou da agenda oficial e foi intermediado pelo ex-ministro Guido Mantega. A reunião foi mencionada por Flávio Bolsonaro durante entrevista ao Jornal Nacional, após o senador ser questionado sobre seus próprios encontros com Vorcaro.

O candidato afirmou que sua relação com o banqueiro era privada, negou ter oferecido qualquer favorecimento e direcionou as críticas a Lula.

“O que não é adequado é um presidente da República recebendo, em uma reunião secreta, um banqueiro, prometendo ajudá-lo a resolver o problema do seu banco. Então, fica a pergunta aqui: quem deve explicações é o Lula”, afirmou Flávio na entrevista.

Em fevereiro de 2026, Lula afirmou que recebeu Vorcaro a pedido, em um compromisso que não constou da agenda oficial do Palácio do Planalto. Segundo o presidente, Mantega foi quem levou o então banqueiro para encontrá-lo.

“Ele então me contou da perseguição que estava sofrendo, que tinha gente interessado em derrubar ele, não sei das quantas...”, disse Lula. “O que eu disse pra ele: ‘não haverá posição política pró ou contra o Banco Master. O que haverá será uma investigação técnica, feita pelo Banco Central’. Foi essa a conversa”, afirmou.

articles.title: Quaest em PE: veja como está a disputa pelo Senado | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada nesta quarta (23) foi encomendada pela Globo. Margem de erro é de três pontos percentuais.
articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada nesta quarta (23) foi encomendada pela Globo. Margem de erro é de três pontos percentuais.
articles.body:
Marília Arraes (PDT), Humberto Costa (PT), Mendonça Filho (PL) e Eduardo da Fonte (PP) — Foto: Andréa Rêgo Barros/Divulgação

Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira (23) mostra como está a disputa pelo Senado em Pernambuco. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo.

Em 2026, serão eleitos dois senadores em cada estado e no Distrito Federal, para renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras. Por isso, cada eleitor precisa votar em dois candidatos diferentes. Não é possível escolher o mesmo nome duas vezes.

Na pesquisa espontânea da Quaest, em que os nomes não são mostrados aos eleitores entrevistados, 73% estão indecisos (eram 78%), porque não souberam citar um candidato.

Já na pesquisa estimulada, a lista de candidatos é mostrada, e cada entrevistado precisa responder duas vezes em quem pretende votar: para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda vaga.

Os resultados da pesquisa para o Senado consideram as menções para a primeira e a segunda vagas em um total que soma 100% das intenções de voto e mantém a proporção entre candidatos, brancos/nulos e indecisos. Veja os números abaixo:

Marília Arraes ( PDT ) : 18% (eram 17% em 8 de setembro);

Pastor Gilvan Costa (Democrata) : 1% (era 1%);

Carlos Sant'anna ( Novo ) : 1% (era 1%);

Paulo Rubem Santiago ( Rede ) : 1% (era 0%);

Branco/nulo/não vai votar : 21% (eram 18%).

articles.title: Homem é preso suspeito de esfaquear motorista que parou para ajudá-lo  | G1
articles.standfirst: Ocorrência foi registrada próximo à UBS da Cohab, em Presidente Prudente (SP). A vítima informou que o passageiro entrou em surto e deu dois golpes de faca no pescoço dela.
articles.summary: Um homem de 36 anos foi preso suspeito de tentativa de homicídio após esfaquear um motorista de 44 anos que tentou ajudá-lo em Presidente Prudente (SP), nesta quarta-feira (23).
articles.body:
Delegacia Seccional de Presidente Prudente — Foto: Polícia Civil/Divulgação

Um homem de 36 anos foi preso suspeito de tentativa de homicídio após esfaquear um motorista de 44 anos que tentou ajudá-lo em Presidente Prudente (SP), na manhã desta quarta-feira (23).

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, o caso começou quando o suspeito caiu na Avenida Salim Farah. O motorista viu a situação e ofereceu ajuda, chegando a levá-lo até uma unidade de saúde.

Na Unidade Básica de Saúde da Cohab, o motorista informou à polícia que o suspeito entrou em surto enquanto estava no veículo e deu dois golpes de faca no pescoço dele. A vítima apresentava intenso sangramento e conseguiu pedir ajuda da equipe médica da unidade.

A Polícia Militar foi acionada. Durante a vistoria do veículo, a equipe localizou a faca que teria sido utilizada na agressão e a carteira do suspeito, com os documentos dele.

O motorista foi encaminhado ao Hospital Regional. Até a publicação desta reportagem, não havia informações sobre o estado de saúde dele.

A Polícia Militar foi até o endereço do suspeito, que havia acabado de chegar ao local. Segundo a corporação, ele confessou ter esfaqueado a vítima.

Ainda conforme a PM, o suspeito disse que faz uso de medicamentos controlados, mas que não havia tomado a medicação naquele dia. Ele também informou que a faca utilizada no crime era a mesma que usava no trabalho, em um açougue.

Diante da situação, o homem foi preso em flagrante e encaminhado à Delegacia de Presidente Prudente (SP).

articles.title: Participação popular no Legislativo: como fiscalizar e propor leis | G1
articles.standfirst: No terceiro e último episódio da série sobre o Poder Legislativo, o RJ2 aborda as formas de participação popular e de fiscalização dos mandatos.
articles.summary: A participação popular no Legislativo permite fiscalizar gastos de mandatos e apresentar projetos de lei diretamente aos parlamentares para fortalecer a transparência pública.
articles.body:
O voto é uma das principais formas de participação política, mas a relação entre eleitores e parlamentares não termina no dia da eleição. A população também pode acompanhar sessões, apresentar sugestões que podem virar projetos de lei e fiscalizar a atuação dos deputados e senadores.

No terceiro e último episódio da série sobre o Poder Legislativo, o RJ2 aborda as formas de participação popular e de fiscalização dos mandatos.

Na Câmara dos Deputados e no Senado, por exemplo, qualquer cidadão pode acompanhar presencialmente as sessões plenárias. As duas Casas mantêm galerias destinadas ao público.

Na Assembleia Legislativa do Rio de Janeiro (Alerj), a população também pode acompanhar as sessões no prédio novo da Casa, inaugurado em 2021. O espaço reservado aos visitantes fica em um mezanino cercado por vidro e permite uma visão parcial do plenário.

Além de acompanhar o trabalho dos parlamentares, o cidadão também pode participar diretamente do processo legislativo, apresentando ideias que podem se transformar em propostas.

Como uma ideia pode virar projeto de lei

Na Alerj, um dos mecanismos de participação popular é o Legisla Aqui, programa que permite que cidadãos apresentem sugestões de projetos de lei.

Em 2022, a Assembleia aprovou o primeiro projeto de lei de autoria popular por meio da iniciativa. A proposta determinou a instalação de composteiras para reaproveitamento de restos de merenda nas escolas da rede estadual.

Praça dos Três Poderes, em Brasília — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

O projeto foi apresentado por três estudantes de Engenharia da Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), que estudavam alternativas para o manejo de resíduos urbanos.

“É uma forma de levar a discussão para o jovem, e o jovem consegue levar para a família”, explicou à época Francisco Victer, um dos autores da proposta.

Para Severino Virgínio, também autor do projeto, a iniciativa permite que a população apresente diretamente aos representantes políticos demandas e propostas para melhorar políticas públicas.

No Senado, também existem mecanismos para que a população participe do processo legislativo. É possível, por exemplo, apresentar ou apoiar ideias legislativas, propostas de emenda à Constituição, medidas provisórias e projetos de lei.

A participação popular também pode ocorrer por meio da fiscalização do trabalho dos parlamentares e do uso do dinheiro público.

Deputados e senadores têm direito a recursos para custear despesas relacionadas ao exercício do mandato. Na Câmara dos Deputados, a Cota para o Exercício da Atividade Parlamentar (Ceap) é usada, entre outras coisas, para despesas com passagens aéreas, hospedagem, combustível e material de escritório.

Na Câmara, a cota varia de acordo com o estado de origem do parlamentar. Os valores citados pelo RJ2 vão de R$ 41.612,55 a R$ 58.086,78.

Essas despesas são públicas e podem ser consultadas pela população. Foi justamente a partir da análise de notas fiscais que o professor Lúcio Big realizou um trabalho de fiscalização dos gastos com combustíveis de parlamentares.

A chamada Operação Tanque Furado analisou mais de mil notas fiscais. Segundo Lúcio, o trabalho resultou na recuperação de mais de R$ 6 milhões aos cofres públicos.

“Falar agora, por exemplo, de Câmara dos Deputados ou Senado Federal: são entidades que prezam pela transparência pública e disponibilizam os documentos à sociedade”, afirmou Lúcio.

Para Clay Sousa Teles, consultor legislativo do Senado, acompanhar o trabalho dos parlamentares é parte da participação democrática.

“O eleitor deve acompanhar o trabalho do seu parlamentar ao longo de todo o mandato”, afirmou.

O acompanhamento do mandato também pode ajudar o eleitor a avaliar a atuação do parlamentar ao longo dos quatro anos.

“O voto é importante, sim. Mas ele não pode ser um fim”, afirmou Guilherme Brandão, diretor-geral da Câmara dos Deputados.

Segundo ele, acompanhar as pautas votadas e a atuação do parlamentar durante o mandato permite ao eleitor refletir, na eleição seguinte, se o representante correspondeu às expectativas que motivaram o voto.

Assim, a participação popular no Legislativo pode acontecer de diferentes formas: acompanhando as sessões, apresentando propostas, apoiando ideias legislativas e fiscalizando a atuação dos parlamentares e o uso dos recursos públicos.

articles.title: Governo Lula avalia como 'muito grave' declaração dos EUA e latinos sobre PCC e CV e vê 'porta de entrada' para militarização | G1
articles.standfirst: Para núcleo diplomático de Lula, acordo do "Escudo das Américas" é manobra dos Estados Unidos para criar agenda punitiva e legitimar ações à revelia do direito internacional.
articles.summary: Para núcleo diplomático de Lula, acordo do "Escudo das Américas" é manobra dos Estados Unidos para criar agenda punitiva e legitimar ações à revelia do direito internacional.
articles.body:
Auxiliares do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) avaliam como “muito grave” o acordo assinado na última terça-feira (22) pelos Estados Unidos e outros 14 países do continente , que incluiu 24 grupos criminosos em uma lista de “organizações narcoterroristas transnacionais”.

Entre os grupos citados estão as facções brasileiras Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) e Comando Vermelho (CV).

Diplomatas avaliam que o documento pode abrir um caminho para uma nova doutrina de segurança dos Estados Unidos na América Latina, com ações duras e com a possibilidade de operações unilaterais na região.

O acordo foi assinado por membros do chamado "Escudo das Américas", uma coalizão lançada pela administração Trump que reúne governos alinhados ao republicano na América Latina, incluindo vizinhos do Brasil, como Argentina, Bolívia e Peru.

responsabilização criminal de pessoas que prestem suporte logístico aos grupos incluídos na lista.

Assinam o texto os membros plenos do Escudo das Américas : Estados Unidos da América, Argentina, Bolívia, Chile, Colômbia, Costa Rica, República Dominicana, Equador, El Salvador, Guiana, Honduras, Panamá, Paraguai, Peru e Trinidad e Tobago.

Embora o governo brasileiro não tenha tido acesso prévio ao texto final da declaração, diplomatas afirmam que a medida não causou surpresa.

Segundo integrantes do governo, movimentações recentes dos Estados Unidos, inclusive no contexto político da Nicarágua, já indicavam que o governo americano pretendia dar mais peso ao combate ao crime organizado em sua relação com os países da região e endurecer a pressão sobre governos latino-americanos.

Na avaliação de membros que acompanham diretamente as negociações em Nova York, a declaração representa uma mudança na forma como os Estados Unidos pretendem se relacionar com a América Latina.

Segundo membros do governo, os Estados Unidos vem combinando três frentes de pressão sobre a região:

abordagem mais militarizada no combate ao narcotráfico.

Para o núcleo diplomático do governo Lula, esse conjunto de medidas poderia servir de base para justificar ações dos Estados Unidos à revelia do direito internacional.

Ciente de que a diplomacia americana estava "cozinhando" a declaração com países aliados, o governo brasileiro preparou uma resposta antecipada. A estratégia foi classificada internamente por assessores presidenciais como uma "vacina tetravalente".

O recado foi levado por Lula à tribuna da Assembleia Geral da Organização das Nações Unidas , antes do discurso do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, e da reunião do Escudo das Américas.

Ao afirmar que o Brasil não vai "terceirizar a responsabilidade de defender nossas fronteiras", que o país "não precisa de porta-aviões" e que o "Brasil não cabe no quintal de ninguém", Lula sinalizou que o governo brasileiro rejeita uma eventual tutela militar estrangeira ou intervenções externas na área de segurança pública nacional.

Para integrantes da diplomacia brasileira, parte dos países aderiu à declaração em razão da pressão exercida pelos Estados Unidos.

Apesar da avaliação crítica sobre o documento, o governo brasileiro não espera, neste momento, mudanças significativas na cooperação de segurança com os países vizinhos.

A expectativa é que o compartilhamento de informações, as ações de inteligência e o combate ao crime nas regiões de fronteira continuem funcionando com base nos acordos bilaterais já existentes.

Na avaliação de diplomatas brasileiros, muitos dos países que assinaram a declaração não têm capacidade operacional para colocar em prática, sozinhos, todas as medidas previstas no documento.

Além disso, o governo considera que esses países têm interesse em preservar as relações políticas e diplomáticas com o Brasil.

A declaração dos países prevê levar o tema para a Organização dos Estados Americanos (OEA). Os países que assinaram o documento pretendem pedir ao Conselho a convocação de uma reunião, com base no Tratado Interamericano de Assistência Recíproca (TIAR).

O objetivo é discutir uma resolução que permita ações coletivas contra os grupos classificados no documento como “narcoterroristas”.

Esse pedido, no entanto, não produz efeitos automaticamente: a convocação precisa ser aprovada pelos países que fazem parte do tratado e, só depois, poderão discutir quais medidas poderiam ser adotadas.

A avaliação de auxiliares do presidente Lula é que ainda não é possível saber quais serão os efeitos práticos da declaração. Isso porque os países pretendem primeiro levar o tema à OEA e fazer uma consulta formal.

Só depois dessa etapa é que eventuais medidas poderão ser discutidas e submetidas à aprovação dos países envolvidos.

articles.title: Fux dá 10 dias para Senado se manifestar em ação sobre visitas | G1
articles.standfirst: Para ministro do STF, a princípio, a divulgação das informações não viola intimidade ou proteção a dados pessoais. Senado alegou esse motivo para não atender solicitação feita por vereador.
articles.summary: Fux deu 10 dias para o Senado justificar o sigilo sobre visitas de Viviane Moraes e Daniel Vorcaro, Para ministro, a princípio, divulgação dos dados não viola a intimidade.
articles.body:
Ministro Luiz Fux durante julgamento no Supremo — Foto: Luiz Silveira/STF

O ministro Luiz Fux, do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), deu nesta quarta-feira (23) prazo de 10 dias para que o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), se manifeste em uma ação que pede a divulgação de registros de entrada e saída no Senado de uma lista de pessoas – que inclui o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro e a esposa do ministro Alexandre de Moraes , a advogada Viviane Barci de Moraes.

Também foram solicitados registros envolvendo José Ferreira da Silva (Frei Chico) e Fábio Luís Lula da Silva – irmão e filho do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), respectivamente – além de Antônio Carlos Camilo Antunes, que é conhecido como "Careca do INSS".

Na avaliação de Fux, "por ora, não se vislumbra violação da intimidade ou de informações pessoais" em atender o pedido.

Esse foi o motivo alegado pelo Senado para não atender ao pedido de um vereador de Curitiba (PR), que solicitou as informações sobre eventuais visitas das pessoas mencionadas na lista.

Na prática, Fux quer saber o motivo que levou o Senado a negar o acesso aos registros desses eventuais registros de entrada e saída e qual a justificativa legal para a medida.

Moraes havia sido escolhido pelo sorteio feito inicialmente pelo sistema do STF. Ele alegou que não podia prosseguir no caso e citou, em despacho, o Código de Processo Civil, que diz que o juiz não pode exercer suas funções em um determinado processo caso um cônjuge seja parte.

Nesta quarta-feira, Fux também determinou que o Ministério Público Federal (MPF) seja ouvido sobre o tema em até 10 dias.

A ação chegou ao STF depois que a Justiça Federal do Paraná se declarou incompetente para cuidar do caso.

O autor do processo é o vereador de Curitiba e candidato a deputado federal Guilherme Kilter (Novo). O presidente do Senado negou os pedidos do parlamentar, alegando proteção a dados pessoais.

Kilter contestou o argumento e disse que a negativa é ilegal e não encontra respaldo na Lei de Acesso à Informação e na Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD), "violando direito líquido e certo de acesso à informação pelo cidadão".

articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada nesta quarta-feira (23) foi encomendada pela TV Anhanguera. Na pesquisa espontânea, em que os nomes dos pré-candidatos não são mostrados aos eleitores, 69% estão indecisos.
articles.summary: Pesquisa divulgada nesta quarta-feira (23) foi encomendada pela TV Anhanguera.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta quarta-feira (23) mostra como está a disputa pelo Senado no Tocantins. O levantamento foi encomendado pela TV Anhanguera.

Em 2026, serão eleitos dois senadores em cada estado e no Distrito Federal (DF), para renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras. Por isso, cada eleitor precisa votar em dois candidatos diferentes. Não é possível escolher o mesmo nome duas vezes.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Na pesquisa espontânea da Quaest — em que os nomes não são mostrados aos eleitores entrevistados —, 69% estão indecisos (era 86% em 25 de agosto), porque não souberam citar um candidato.

Já na pesquisa estimulada, a lista de candidatos é mostrada, e cada entrevistado precisa responder duas vezes em quem pretende votar: para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda vaga.

articles.title: Roberta Luchsinger pagou servidores de ministério; pasta contratou empresário ligado a ela seis meses depois | G1
articles.standfirst: A defesa da empresária afirmou que não se manifestaria "sobre vazamentos ilegais". Em nota, o Ministério do Desenvolvimento Social, local de trabalho dos servidores, negou favorecimento em licitação.
articles.summary: A defesa da empresária afirmou que não se manifestaria "sobre vazamentos ilegais". Em nota, o Ministério do Desenvolvimento Social, local de trabalho dos servidores, negou favorecimento em licitação.
articles.body:
A empresária Roberta Luchsinger é alvo de três inquéritos — Foto: Reprodução

A Polícia Federal (PF) identificou que a lobista Roberta Luchsinger ordenou que seu motorista fizesse pagamentos em dinheiro vivo a dois servidores do Ministério do Desenvolvimento Social.

Os depósitos foram em 2023 para o secretário-executivo adjunto do ministério, Ranniêr Costa Ciríaco, e para coordenador do cerimonial do ministro do Desenvolvimento Social, Wellington Dias, José Martinho Ferreira de Araújo.

O ministério fechou um contrato com um empresário de tecnologia representado por Roberta seis meses após os pagamentos.

A informação foi revelada pelo jornal o Estado de S. Paulo. A TV Globo também teve acesso.

Roberta é investigada em conjunto com Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, o Lulinha, filho mais velho do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), em três inquéritos sob suspeita de corrupção e tráfico de influência.

A defesa da empresária afirmou que não se manifestaria "sobre vazamentos ilegais e sem a mínima comprovação, que servem apenas para efeito eleitoral as vésperas do sufrágio".

Em nota, o Ministério do Desenvolvimento Social negou "que tenha havido qualquer tipo de favorecimento na licitação de serviços de backup de tecnologia, que foi realizada por meio de pregão eletrônico - modalidade em que vence a empresa a apresentar o menor preço durante disputa feita com absoluta transparência".

Ainda de acordo com o minsitério, os servidores citados não tem competência sobre essa área, "logo não houve qualquer participação no processo licitatório em questão".

Os pagamentos foram levantados pela PF a partir de mensagens encontradas no celular da lobista.

Os investigadores relatam que no dia 2 de junho de 2023 Roberta pede que Ulisses Barbosa, seu auxiliar pessoal e motorista, vá até seu quarto e pegue uma sacola com dinheiro e separe R$ 60 mil. A conversa começa no fim da manhã.

Ulisses chegou a alertar que "esse montante tem que ser diluído para depositar... pq o banco faz uma série de questionamentos.

Em reposta, a lobista afirma: "são em várias contas". Depois, há uma sequência de mensagens apagadas.

Roberta então informa duas contas e pede que sejam depositados R$ 20 mil em cada uma.

No início da tarde, Roberta escreve para o auxiliar pedindo que também seja repassado R$ 20 mil para uma terceira conta e questiona: "Ontem deixaram um pacote ai ? Se sim, vc faz mais 20 nessa".

Os dados são de contas de Ranniêr, José Martinho e a uma parente dele.

Mensagens de Roberta Luchsinger para Ulisses Barbosa — Foto: Reprodução

Cerca de uma hora depois de receber os números das contas, o motorista informa que está no banco e que foi alertado de que valores acima de R$ 50 mil destinados a um CPF entram na mira do Banco Central. "Já aciona tipo um alerta lá. Só avisando", escreveu.

Depois envia os comprovantes dos depósitos de R$ 20 mil e "feito".

A PF afirma que é preciso aprofundar a análise das movimentações financeiras diante das investigações em andamento contra Roberta e seu grupo.

Comprovante de transferência para Ranniêr Costa Ciríaco e para José Martinho Ferreira de Araújo — Foto: Reprodução

Os investigadores destacam, por exemplo, que Ulisses é responsável por intensas movimentações de valores para Roberta.

Eles dizem ainda que o auxiliar movimentou valores elevados em sua conta corrente. Segundo as investigações, "entre 2022 e 2025, a empresa de Roberta transferiu quase R$2.300.000,00 para a conta de Ulisses, Ulisses transferiu entre 2022 e 2023 pouco mais de R$130.000,00 para a conta da RL".

articles.title: Débora do Batom: PGR defende regime semiaberto para condenada | G1
articles.standfirst: Em manifestação enviada ao STF, Paulo Gonet afirmou que a cabeleireira Débora Rodrigues, que está em prisão domiciliar, já preencheu requisitos para obter o benefício. Ela foi condenada a 14 anos por participação nos atos golpistas de 8 de Janeiro.
articles.summary: Paulo Gonet afirmou ao STF que a cabeleireira Débora Rodrigues, condenada a 14 anos pelos atos de 8 de Janeiro, já preencheu os requisitos legais para o benefício.
articles.body:
A Procuradoria-Geral da República defendeu nesta quarta-feira (23) a concessão, pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), da progressão para o regime semiaberto para a cabeleireira Débora Rodrigues dos Santos, a "Débora do Batom". Atualmente, ela cumpre a pena em prisão domiciliar.

🔎O regime semiaberto é uma modalidade de cumprimento de pena privativa de liberdade intermediária entre o regime fechado e o aberto. No semiaberto, a pessoa condenada cumpre parte da pena em trabalho externo no período diurno, devendo retornar ao local da prisão para o recolhimento noturno e nos dias de folga.

Débora foi condena a 14 anos de prisão por participação nos atos golpistas do 8 de Janeiro de 2023 . A pena foi fixada da seguinte forma:

abolição Violenta do Estado Democrático de Direito : 4 anos e 6 meses de prisão; na lei, a pena varia de 4 a 8 anos.

golpe de Estado : 5 anos de prisão; na lei, a pena varia de 4 a 12 anos;

️dano qualificado : 1 ano e 6 meses de prisão; na lei, a pena varia de 6 meses a 3 anos de prisão.

️deterioração do patrimônio tombado : 1 ano e 6 meses de prisão; na lei, a pena varia de 1 a 3 anos.

️associação criminosa armada : 1 ano e 6 meses de prisão; na lei, a pena varia de 1 a 3 anos de prisão.

Ela ficou conhecida por ter pichado, no dia dos atos golpistas, "perdeu, mané" na estátua "A Justiça", que fica em frente à sede do STF.

Em manifestação enviada ao Supremo, o procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet , afirmou que ela já cumpre os requisitos para o regime semiaberto.

A Procuradoria afirma que a cabeleireira já cumpriu 1.287 dias de pena, considerando 742 dias da prisão preventiva e ainda obteve o perdão de 2 dias de pena.

"Verifica-se, assim, que a apenada alcançou a fração mínima legalmente prevista para a pena imposta (requisito objetivo)", declarou Gonet no despacho encaminhado ao STF.

"Quanto ao requisito subjetivo, não há registro de falta disciplinar cometida, nem violação às medidas cautelares impostas em período posterior ao deferimento da prisão domiciliar. Assim, não há óbice ao reconhecimento do cumprimento do requisito subjetivo, mostrando-se possível a concessão da progressão de regime", concluiu o procurador-geral.

Débora Rodrigues dos Santos foi condenada pelo STF por crimes como associação criminosa armada e golpe de Estado — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: André Marinho planeja polo econômico e menos burocracia no Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato ao governo do Rio de Janeiro pelo Partido Novo esteve no Cadeg Mercado Municipal do Rio de Janeiro nesta quarta-feira (23).
articles.summary: André Marinho, candidato ao governo do Rio pelo Novo, visitou o Cadeg e detalhou planos para facilitar negócios e aumentar a segurança no Arco Metropolitano.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do Rio de Janeiro pelo Partido Novo, André Marinho, esteve no Cadeg Mercado Municipal do Rio de Janeiro nesta quarta-feira (23).

O candidato apresentou aos comerciantes e funcionários alguns dos pontos do seu plano de governo para o desenvolvimento econômico do estado.

André Marinho disse que, se for eleito, vai implantar um programa para simplificar a burocracia e facilitar o ambiente de negócios, unificando tributos e processos, e aperfeiçoando a comunicação entre as secretarias de governo.

O candidato disse, ainda, que pretende reforçar a segurança do Arco Metropolitano e criar um polo econômico com oferta de novos empregos ao longo da rodovia, entre os municípios de Itaguaí e Itaboraí, além de melhorar a infraestrutura de armazenamento, processamento e distribuição por onde escoa a produção.

André Marinho promete implantar programa para simplificar burocracia e facilitar ambiente de negócios — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

" Para que o consumidor carioca possa incorporar no seu dia a dia e comprar pelo menor valor possível, mas também para os comerciantes da Cadeg terem mais dinheiro no bolso e poderem se sentir protagonistas. A gente precisa dessa clareza moral e dessa inteligência operacional", comentou.

O candidato afirmou ainda que pretende reduzir o ICMS de 22% para os patamares dos outros estados do sudeste que praticam alíquotas entre 17% e 18%.

articles.title: Gov. Greg Abbott faces growing challenge in Texas governor's race
articles.summary: Abbott still leads the latest Texas governor poll, but two forecasters now rate the race a toss-up as Hinojosa narrows the gap. See what's shifting.
articles.body:
The Texas governor's race is starting to look less safe for Republicans, with two election forecasters moving it toward a toss-up as polling trends edge toward Democrats.

Fox News updated its power rankings on Sept. 22 for the 2026 midterm elections and shifted the race between Gov. Greg Abbott and Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa from "likely Republican" to "lean Republican."

The news outlet cited data center construction's impact on resources and residents' concerns as a top issue for Texans as they head to the polls on Nov. 3.

This movement also comes after RealClearPolitics on Sept. 17, a polling data aggregator, moved the race between Abbott and Hinojosa from Republican leaning to a toss up.

The data aggregator shows that since April 29, 2026, Hinojosa has cut Abbott's average poll lead from 7 percentage points down to 2.2 percentage points as of Sept. 22.

A month ago, the Cook Political Report moved the race from "Solid Republican" to "Likely Republican" for several reasons—mainly because Abbott wasn't spending much money on attack ads at the time.

This shift follows a recent poll released by Texas Southern University released on Sept. 22 shows that Abbott leads Hinojosa by 4 percentage points, 49%-45%.

Here's what the poll shows and how it compares with the rest of the September polls.

Greg Abbott leads Gina Hinojosa in Texas governor's race

The TSU poll was conducted Sept. 15-19 and surveyed 1,800 Texans likely to vote in the November 2026 election, with a margin of error of 2.31 percentage points.

It found that 99% of likely voters know enough about Abbott to have an opinion of him. In contrast, only 79% of voters know enough about Hinojosa to have an opinion of her.

The poll also found that Abbott has a slight negative favorability rating, viewed favorably by 49% of likely voters and unfavorably by 50%. Hinojosa has a positive favorability rating, being viewed favorably by 42% and unfavorably by 37%.

Here is a look at how the different voter groups are breaking in the race, according to the poll:

Latino voters: Hinojosa 57%, Abbott 40%.

On voter age, Abbott leads 60% to 36% among likely voters age 55 and older. Meanwhile, Hinojosa leads 50% to 44% among likely voters ages 35 to 54 and 71% to 21% among likely voters under 35.

Here's a look at recent September polling as the race enters its final stretch:

Emerson College Polling (Sept. 17 ) — Abbott 49%, Hinojosa 46%.

ReconMR Texas poll (Sept. 17) — Hinojosa 49%, Abbott 45%.

Mason-Dixon Polling (Sept. 15) — Abbott 48%, Hinojosa 41%.

SoCal Strategies (Sept. 13) — Abbott 52%, Hinojosa 44%.

N+ Univision (Sept. 9) — Abbott 47%, Hinojosa 47%.

articles.title: How US states mistakenly added 30,000 non-citizens to voter rolls
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Sept 23 (Reuters) - US states may have added more than 30,000 self-declared non-citizens to the nation’s voter rolls since 2000 because of softwa...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Sept 23 (Reuters) - US states may have added more than 30,000 self-declared non-citizens to the nation's voter rolls since 2000 because of software glitches and clerical errors made while processing their driver's license and state ID applications, according to official records reviewed by Reuters.

The cases expose weaknesses in voter registration systems across a dozen US states governed by both Democrats and Republicans, but at numbers that experts said were too small relative to the country's more than 170 million registered voters to impact elections. Reuters was not ‌able to determine how many of these non-citizens actually cast a ballot.

The findings suggest that inadvertent bureaucratic failures, rather than organized efforts to register immigrants illegally, are a major source of non-citizen registrations, and raise questions about whether legislative efforts to require proof of citizenship for voter registration ‌would eliminate the issue.

President Donald Trump and his supporters have claimed, without evidence, that non-citizen voting is widespread and part of an organized conspiracy led by Democrats who hope to retake Congress in November's midterm elections, and are pushing lawmakers to toughen up voting requirements.

New Jersey announced the most recent high-profile case of errant voter registrations over the summer, saying a technology glitch added about 6,600 non-citizens ​to voter rolls between June 2023 and June 2024, even though they answered "no" when asked if they were citizens while applying for licenses and IDs.

Bureaucratic errors have also been reported in at least 11 other states – including Republican strongholds like Iowa, Texas and South Dakota - bringing the nationwide figure above 30,000 since 2000, according to the Reuters reporting.

A nationwide tally of such mistakes has not previously been reported.

Reuters used data from the Center for Election Innovation & Research, a non-profit group that tracks claims of non-citizen voter registration and voting, to identify states where self-declared non-citizens were registered. Reuters then verified the numbers with state officials, court records, and local media reports.

The data showed errors occurred in California, Illinois, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Dakota, Texas, Utah and Virginia.

The numbers are inexact because state data is often tentative and subject to revision.

Such mistakes are likely a top reason non-citizens make it onto the nation's voter rolls, according to Don Palmer, a senior legal fellow for election integrity at the conservative Heritage Foundation and former Trump-appointed ‌chair of the US Election Assistance Commission.

"I think that's the primary issue," Palmer said. "Driver's license agencies often make mistakes, ⁠and they often are not taking this as seriously as election officials." He said states also need to do more to verify voter eligibility.

The White House has pressured Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, a proposal to crack down on illegal voting that would require people to show proof of US citizenship to register to vote, and a photo ID to cast a ballot.

But it is unlikely such a bill would prevent the kinds of mistakes being made by state agencies, said David Becker, executive ⁠director of CEIR.

"In each of these instances, the individual did exactly what they were supposed to do. If there was some requirement that you had to show proof of citizenship, these problems would still exist, because the processes themselves failed," he said.

Proponents of the SAVE America Act say it is a common-sense way to ensure only eligible voters can cast ballots. Most states don't require documented proof of citizenship.

Critics counter that the legislation's restrictions could disenfranchise millions of voters who lack easy access to passports or birth certificates, including low-income people and racial minorities, while creating unnecessary turmoil for the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

"This is not a problem," said Elaine Kamarck, an expert on governance at the Brookings Institution. "There's just no evidence that ​massive ​numbers of non-citizens are voting."

Immigrants do sometimes make false declarations about their citizenship in order to be registered to vote in US elections, according to the Department of Justice. But there ​is no evidence to show it is widespread.

A Reuters data analysis published earlier this year showed federal prosecutors have charged ‌only 129 people under a federal "voting by aliens" statute created by Congress in 1996. In none of those cases did prosecutors allege a coordinated effort to influence an election.

The White House said non-citizen voter registrations were proof that US elections have been compromised and cited 11 arrests of non-citizens for illegal voting announced by federal authorities since May.

"The real story here is after decades of the media denying that non-citizens register and vote in our elections, they are finally being forced to admit after a flurry of recent arrests nationwide that it does happen," White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said in a statement.

Underlying the glitches and human errors are state motor-voter systems that register people to vote when they apply for driver's licenses, state IDs and other government services under the National Voter Registration Act.

The largely Democratic initiative to address low voter participation passed in 1993 with bipartisan support under then-President Bill Clinton. Voter registration has climbed to more than 86% in 2024, from 62% in 1990, according to Census data and the US Election Assistance Commission.

Republicans claim that such state motor-voter systems have become a major problem, however, due to the doubling of the US immigrant population since 1990.

Automatically registering people to vote in this way "is irrational when you realize people that are not citizens in the United States are getting ‌driver's licenses," said US Representative Bryan Steil, a Wisconsin Republican who oversees federal election policy as chair of the House Administration Committee.

All 50 states allow legal immigrants to obtain driver's ​licenses, while 19 US states and the District of Columbia also provide driver's licenses to undocumented immigrants.

Randall Marquis, a Canadian who lives in California, remembers the day when he got ​a card in the mail notifying him that he was registered to vote in the 2018 midterm elections during Trump's first term.

"I just said, 'Well, this ​is stupid.' So, I put it aside. But after thinking about it, I decided, no, it's more than stupid. This is bad!" the 71-year-old green card holder told Reuters.

He alerted news organizations, and state officials later disclosed that as many as 1,500 non-citizens had ‌been mistakenly registered to vote by the California Department of Motor Vehicles due to a processing error, according to media ​reports.

State officials did not respond to Reuters queries seeking confirmation.

Similar problems have happened in ​Oregon where hundreds of immigrants who presented foreign passports and birth certificates were registered to vote because of clerical mistakes at the Department of Motor Vehicles, according to state records.

DMV officials also registered hundreds of American Samoans who presented US passports, not realizing that people from the US territory are nationals but not citizens, and therefore not eligible to vote.

In some other states, estimates of registered non-citizens have been initially overstated.

Just before the 2024 election, Iowa, for example, announced that more than 2,000 people had registered to vote or had voted in the state after self-reporting to the Iowa ​Department of Transportation as non-citizens.

Six months later, the number shrank to 277.

Iowa state officials said 35 non-citizens cast ballots that ‌were counted in the 2024 general election. Overall, more than 1.6 million Iowans voted in that election.

The problems are bigger elsewhere. Since 2014, Virginia has reported hundreds of non-citizens each year on its voter rolls who identified themselves as foreign nationals, with a total of more ​than 4,500 in 2025 alone, according to annual reports by the state Department of Elections.

State officials say those numbers include people who later became citizens, and others who were stricken off the rolls.

Palmer of the Heritage Foundation said states should be required to address the issue.

"There's ​an obligation to fix the problem. So, take the politics out, and fix the problem," he said.

(Reporting by David Morgan; editing by Michael Learmonth and Richard Valdmanis)

articles.title: Iran's president tells Trump it will never 'bend the knee'
articles.summary: Masoud Pezeshkian's defiant speech to the UN comes after the US president threatened to "annihilate" Iran if a peace deal is not agreed soon.
articles.body:
President Masoud Pezeshkian has said Iran will never "bend the knee" after almost seven months of war with the US and Israel, but is ready for a diplomatic solution to the conflict.

Responding to US President Donald Trump's threat to "annihilate" the Islamic Republic if a deal is not reached soon, he told the UN General Assembly: "The resistance of the Iranian people will only increase in the face of sanctions, increased pressure, increased bullying."

Pezeshkian also insisted any deal would have to include an end to the US blockade stopping Iranian ships from using a key Gulf waterway.

"It cannot be the case that everyone benefits from the Strait of Hormuz while we are denied access," he said.

There was no immediate comment from the US, whose delegation walked out of the chamber at the start of Pezeshkian's address.

"The US president described us as terrorists. We have been the victims of terrorism," Iran's president told the UN in New York.

He then held up a photo of the country's late Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in a strike on his residence when the US and Israel launched a joint attack in late February.

He also presented pictures of some of the more than 175 civilians, two thirds of them children, who Iranian authorities say were killed in missile strikes on a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd that day. The US has denied striking Lamerd and said it is still investigating what happened in Minab.

"Our innocent people have been the targets of cowardly attacks and aggressions imposed on our country. And we defended ourselves with utmost strength," Pezeshkian said.

Also on Wednesday, an attack on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz killed an Indian sailor, the Agence France-Presse news agency reported, citing Omani and Indian authorities.

The attack was condemned by India's foreign ministry, which called for unimpeded passage through the Strait to be restored.

In February, Iran retaliated for the massive US-Israeli air campaign by launching deadly missile and drone attacks on Israel and neighbouring Gulf Arab states which host US military bases.

It also effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, by attacking commercial vessels in the Gulf, the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. The US responded by imposing a blockade of Iranian ports and ships in April.

In June, the US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait, but it collapsed within weeks after the Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

Iran wants to retain some measure of control over the strait and collect fees from vessels that use it, which the US has rejected.

Watch: Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran if no deal reached

In his address to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, Trump said he faced a "big decision" - either negotiate a deal that would allow Iranians to rebuild their country, or "annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly".

Pezeshkian said the threat was "a sign of a bullying mentality".

"[Trump] must know that the resistance of the Iranian people will only increase in the face of sanctions, increased pressure, increased bullying. We will never bow our head or bend the knee," he said.

But he added: "We are ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations without accepting the language of force."

Pezeshkian made clear that the US blockade would have to end as part of any deal.

"It cannot be the case that everyone benefits from the Strait of Hormuz while we are denied access to shipping through this waterway," he said.

He also reiterated that Iran would not give up its right to have a civilian nuclear programme and that it would not seek to develop nuclear weapons.

"We say it clearly: no nuclear weapons and no limitations on peaceful nuclear technology."

Trump argued in his speech that the war had prevented Iran from obtaining a nuclear bomb and demanded that its leaders "relinquish their nuclear ambitions".

On Tuesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US envoy Steve Witkoff held indirect talks brokered by Qatari mediators on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.

Witkoff said he hoped the discussions – the first since June – would "prove constructive and promising", adding that the mediators would continue their work.

But Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baqai said the talks were "not anything new" and that Araghchi had maintained Iran's conditions, including the end of the US blockade and the release of frozen Iranian assets.

articles.title: US lawmakers seek sanctions for Israel’s ‘E1’ West Bank settlement plan
articles.summary: Project would effectively cleave Palestinian territory in half and has prompted widespread international condemnation.
articles.body:
A group of lawmakers in the United States Senate are seeking sanctions against facilitators of Israel’s controversial “E1” settlement programme .

The legislation introduced on Wednesday calls for punitive actions against individuals and groups that support the settlement project, which would link the Ma’ale Adumim and other illegal Israeli settlements to occupied East Jerusalem.

The plan would completely sever East Jerusalem, long seen as the capital of a future Palestinian state, from the West Bank, while effectively cleaving the overall territory in two. The project, if completed, has been seen by supporters and detractors alike as a death blow to future Palestinian statehood.

19 Democrats co-sponsored the bill, which was spearheaded by Chris Coons of ‌Delaware, Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, Ron Wyden of Oregon and Ruben Gallego of Arizona.

“As Palestinian civilians face a campaign of devastation and fear from violent extremist settlers, the United States must send a strong message that this behaviour is unacceptable and that it remains committed to freedom, security, prosperity and self-determination for all Israelis and Palestinians,” Coons said in a statement.

The bill will impose sanctions “on any foreign person that the Secretary of the Treasury determines to have been responsible for or complicit in the construction of any Israeli settlements or related structures in the E1 area of the West Bank, including by submitting a bid for E1 tenders”, according to a statement from the lawmakers.

“It would also impose sanctions on those who attempt to organise, direct, finance, or facilitate the transfer of Israeli civilians into E1 settlements,” the statement said.

The move is yet another indication of growing discontent among some US lawmakers over Israel’s policies towards the occupied Palestinian territory, including its genocidal war in Gaza and the state-backed expansion of illegal settlements across the West Bank, where settler pogroms, often under the protection of Israeli forces, has surged in recent years.

The criticism has been particularly acute among Democrats, who are seeking to take control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate in the midterm elections in November. A handful of Republicans have also increasingly questioned the close ties between the US and Israel and the unconditional military aid provided by Washington.

Beyond Wednesday’s bill, a growing number of Democrats have voted to block arms transfers to Israel in recent months. More than 20 Democrats in the 100-member Senate also recently introduced a resolution calling for an investigation into surging West Bank violence, in which at least nine US citizens have been killed.

Criticism of the E1 settlement project, short for “East 1”, the Israeli administrative name for the area, escalated last month when the Israeli government invited bids for building 1,200 new units.

The move has come shortly before Israel is set to hold elections in October and is considered by some analysts to be an effort to mobilise the right-wing base of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyu by provoking an international response. The project has been spearheaded by far-right minister Bezalel Smotrich, himself from an illegal settlement.

Among those condemning the plan was UK Foreign Minister Ed Miliband, who has called the project an “unacceptable and destructive act”. Countries across the Middle East, North America and Europe have also voiced strong objections.

The United Nations Human Rights Office has described the E1 project as a “grave and unlawful step to consolidate annexation”.

The administration of US President Donald Trump, for its part, has not directly addressed the plan, instead reiterating opposition to Israeli annexation of the West Bank.

articles.title: Don Lemon on Trump banning CNN: ‘It’s their own fault’
articles.summary: Pundit Don Lemon suggested CNN was at fault for President Trump banning the network and two other media outlets from the White House last week. “It’s their own fault,” Lemon said of the network that fired him in 2023. “They sort of ushered this in by bending the knee and putting on MAGA folks.” Lemon…
articles.body:
Pundit Don Lemon suggested CNN was at fault for President Trump banning the network and two other media outlets from the White House last week.

“It’s their own fault,” Lemon said of the network that fired him in 2023. “They sort of ushered this in by bending the knee and putting on MAGA folks.”

Lemon suggested recent efforts by CNN’s editorial leadership to put forth a more politically diverse set of viewpoints in its commentary and analysis was an attempt to appease the administration.

“For Donald Trump, there is no loyalty. Just because you do something for him … that doesn’t mean he’s going to be nice to you,” Lemon said. “He’s going to kick you out of the White House right along with everyone else who doesn’t write favorable things about him no matter how much you kiss his a–.”

Trump has long railed against CNN, and on Friday, included it in a list of three media outlets banned from the White House over publishing of “fake news.”

The trio filed a lawsuit Monday over the ban, saying it violates their First Amendment rights to report on the president, while the administration argues their reporting puts national security in danger.

Lemon, a longtime figure in cable news, has since started his own media company and online show since being fired by the network in 2023.

A frequent critic of the president and conservatives, Lemon was recently hit with a felony indictment by the Trump administration, charging the former CNN anchor with federal civil rights and conspiracy crimes in connection with his reporting on an anti-Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) protest at a Minnesota church.
